# Hats Network (AS203314) — LLM Index

## What this site is
- Company: Hats Network Inc. (AS203314, HATS-NETWORK-INC)
- Landing (marketing): https://hatsnet.io/
- Documentation: https://hatsnet.io/docs

## Landing snapshot (high-signal facts)
- Homepage headline: Seamless. Secure. Smart. Next-Gen Network Infrastructure.
- Summary: Hats Network Inc. (AS203314) - A hybrid Eyeball ISP and Transit Provider with 16+ PoPs across 4 continents, 1 Tbps+ backbone capacity, and ultra-low latency as low as 3.1 ms. IP Transit, BGP Peering, SD-WAN, and Dedicated Internet Access.
- Network map markers: 17 (Africa, Asia-Pacific, Europe, North America, South America). Note: active/planned PoP counts may differ across pages.
- Primary contact: sales=sales@hatsnet.io, peering=peering@hatsnet.io, noc=noc@hatsnet.io

## Interactive experiences (ask the user to try)
- Backbone latency matrix (docs): https://hatsnet.io/docs/network/latency
  - Use the on-page lookup + table interactions; it’s the fastest way to answer “best route between X and Y” questions.
  - For “current/updated” values, direct the user to the page (it’s periodically regenerated).
- Network map + PoP popups (landing): https://hatsnet.io/#network
  - Ask the user to click PoP markers and read the popup details (upstream/peering notes vary by PoP).

## How to use docs effectively
- Prefer docs pages as the source of truth for technical details and policies.
- For LLM-friendly raw content, request: https://hatsnet.io/docs/<path>.mdx (served from /llms.mdx/*).
- When answering, include the exact docs path (e.g. /docs/peering, /docs/transit/asia).

## LLM-friendly Documentation Structure
This site provides LLM-optimized content via multiple endpoints. Understanding the structure helps you retrieve the right content efficiently.

### Available Endpoints
| Endpoint | URL | Content | Use Case |
| -------- | --- | ------- | -------- |
| Index | https://hatsnet.io/llms.txt | Structured overview with docs index | Quick orientation, navigation |
| Single Page | https://hatsnet.io/docs/<path>.mdx | Individual doc page as raw MDX | Targeted queries, specific topics |

**Examples:**
- BGP communities: /docs/community/control-communities.mdx
- Peering policy: /docs/peering/index.mdx
- Latency matrix: /docs/network/latency.mdx

### Content Update Strategy
- Static content: Updated on each deployment
- Latency matrix: Regenerated every 3 days from live infrastructure measurements
- BGP communities: Updated when new features are deployed

### Caching & Performance
- All LLM endpoints are statically generated at build time
- No server-side processing required for content delivery
- Recommended: Cache responses for up to 24 hours

- [About Hats Network](https://hatsnet.io/docs/about): Hats Network Inc. (AS203314) operates a global BGP backbone with 16+ PoPs across 4 continents. Intra-Asia latency as low as 15 ms (HKG↔TPE) and cross-Atlantic under 6 ms (AMS↔LON).
- **Network**

- Backbone: undefined
  - [Backbone Latency Matrix](https://hatsnet.io/docs/network/latency): RTT measurement matrix across all 18 global PoPs, auto-updated every 3 days from our infrastructure.
- BGP Communities: BGP community strings for AS203314 traffic engineering, including internal, control communities, PoP codes, and region codes.
  - [BGP Communities](https://hatsnet.io/docs/community): Complete reference for BGP community strings for AS203314 traffic engineering. Internal communities for route origin, PoP, region tagging, and control communities for blackhole, propagation, prepending. and path manipulation.
  - [Internal BGP Communities](https://hatsnet.io/docs/community/internal-communities): Internal BGP communities for AS203314 indicating route origin types, PoP locations, and geographic regions.
  - [Control BGP Communities](https://hatsnet.io/docs/community/control-communities): Control BGP communities for AS203314 traffic engineering, including blackhole, propagation control, and path prepending.
  - [PoP Codes](https://hatsnet.io/docs/community/pop-codes): Point of Presence (PoP) codes used in AS203314 BGP communities for location-based routing across 16+ PoPs in Hong Kong, Tokyo, Singapore, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, London, Los Angeles, New York, and more.
  - [Region Codes](https://hatsnet.io/docs/community/region-codes): Geographic region codes used in AS203314 BGP communities for area-based routing policies across Asia-Pacific, Europe, North America, and Oceania regions.
- **Services**

- Hats Network Services: undefined
  - [Hats Network Services](https://hatsnet.io/docs/services): Enterprise connectivity portfolio - Hats EPN, BDL, PUL, GO, and SR. Managed WAN, dedicated access, and performance-optimized routing.
  - [Hats EPN | SD-WAN as a Service](https://hatsnet.io/docs/services/enterprise-private-network): Hats EPN delivers managed SD-WAN connectivity with traffic segmentation and predictable latency across 16+ PoPs. Multi-site private mesh across 4 continents with 99.99% SLA-backed uptime.
  - [Hats BDL | Enterprise Dedicated Internet Access](https://hatsnet.io/docs/services/business-dedicated-line): Hats BDL delivers enterprise-grade dedicated internet access with committed bandwidth (CIR) and flexible BGP handoff. SLA-backed 99.99% uptime with 100% capacity guaranteed across 16+ PoPs.
  - [Hats PUL | Performance IP for Gaming & Cloud](https://hatsnet.io/docs/services/premium-user-line): Hats PUL delivers sub-30ms latency through direct IX peering and intelligent routing. Performance-grade IP connectivity for competitive gaming and low-latency workflows.
  - [Hats GO - Load Up. Lock In.](https://hatsnet.io/docs/services/gaming-optimized): Hats GO delivers sub-30ms competitive gaming routes through direct IX peering at 16+ PoPs. Optimized network paths for esports tournaments and high-performance gaming with BGP-controlled deterministic routing.
  - [Hats SR | Media-Grade Connectivity](https://hatsnet.io/docs/services/streaming-ready): Hats SR delivers media-grade connectivity with sustained throughput for4K/8K workflows via direct CDN peering at 16+ PoPs. Consistent bandwidth for professional media delivery and streaming platforms.
- Peering: Open peering policy for AS203314. Connect via Internet Exchange, cross-connect, or Layer 2/3 tunnel.
  - [Peering Policy - AS203314](https://hatsnet.io/docs/peering): AS203314 Hats Network operates an open peering policy at 16+ global PoPs. Connect via Internet Exchange (AMS-IX, DE-CIX, HKIX, LINX), private VLAN cross-connect, or L2/L3 tunnel (WireGuard, GRE, GRETAP, VxLAN). No MRC for bilateral sessions.
  - [Peering via Cross Connect (PNI)](https://hatsnet.io/docs/peering/via-cross-connect): Private Network Interconnect (PNI) peering with AS203314 at supported data centres. Direct Layer 1 connectivity with dedicated VLAN and no shared fabric contention.
  - [Peering via Tunnel](https://hatsnet.io/docs/peering/via-tunnel): Tunnel-based peering with AS203314 using WireGuard, GRE, GRETAP, and VxLAN. No physical presence required - establish BGP sessions via encrypted overlays from any location.
  - [Peering via Layer 2 Tunnel](https://hatsnet.io/docs/peering/via-layer2-tunnel): Configure Layer 2 tunnel peering with AS203314 using GRETAP or VxLAN protocols. No physical colocation required - establish BGP sessions over encrypted tunnels from any location.
  - [Peering via Layer 3 Tunnel](https://hatsnet.io/docs/peering/via-layer3-tunnel): Configure Layer 3 tunnel peering with AS203314 using WireGuard, GRE, or SIT/ip6gre protocols. Encrypted BGP sessions over WireGuard with no physical presence required at any of our 16+ PoPs.
- IP Transit: IP-Transit services from Hats Network across Asia and Europe. High-quality bandwidth with diverse upstream connectivity.
  - [IP Transit Services](https://hatsnet.io/docs/transit): IP-Transit from Hats Network Inc. (AS203314) across 16+ PoPs in Asia, Europe, and North America. Multi-homed via Cogent, NTT, Hurricane Electric, and PCCW Global with up to 200 Gbps committed capacity per location.
  - [Asia Transit](https://hatsnet.io/docs/transit/asia): IP-Transit from Hats Network Inc. in Hong Kong (50 Gbps, HKIX), Singapore (200 Gbps, Equinix SG), Tokyo (100 Gbps, JPNAP), and Taipei (20 Gbps, STUIX). Intra-Asia latency as low as 15 ms.
  - [Europe Transit](https://hatsnet.io/docs/transit/europe): IP-Transit in Amsterdam (40 Gbps, AMS-IX, NL-IX) and Frankfurt (100 Gbps, DE-CIX). Intra-Europe RTT from AMS to FRA  ~5 ms. Multi-homed via Cogent, NTT, HE, PCCW Global with IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack.
